answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce stake, then slash it when independently checked actions reveal coordinated fraud; reputation and access grow only after costly, verified work. Sybils can still appear, but they cannot cheaply multiply influence: the attacker must immobilize capital per identity and risk losing it. A river of cheap accounts therefore hits a yarrow-like filter of repeated audits, while the nadir of trust after a failed check makes rebuilding costly. The defense raises the price of attack, rather than proving one person per account.
